canonical_input_state.buyer_accessibility: viable general route; no named buyer

significance_decision.reason: GBS Africa sells research-led advisory, market-entry, partnership and institutional communications services and is actively publishing 2026 analysis. Its research authority is therefore commercially relevant to the published operating model. The current binary-only distribution, missing structured data, broken reports path and weak entity disambiguation affect a core authority asset rather than a peripheral page.

offer_hypothesis_test.reason: A whole-library sprint is larger than needed to prove value. One flagship-report pilot plus a reusable pattern is the smallest credible entry engagement.

entry_offer.name: Flagship Research Citability and Entity Clarity Pilot
entry_offer.core_problem: GBS Africa's current research can be downloaded but is difficult for search and AI systems to cite, attribute and connect unambiguously to the London advisory firm.
entry_offer.desired_outcome: Turn one current flagship report into a citable, attributable HTML authority page and establish a reusable entity and report pattern for later library expansion.
exact_scope: Use Africa Prospects 2026 as the pilot report.
Create one HTML landing-page specification with title, executive summary, named author, publication date, key findings, source references, canonical URL and direct link to the original PDF.
Define and validate Report or Article structured data for the pilot page and Organization structured data with approved sameAs links for GBS Africa.

Add an explicit entity-disambiguation specification covering legal name, trading name, London headquarters, Nairobi office and official profiles without claiming the unrelated gbsafrica.net company is affiliated.
Specify repair of the broken Reports navigation destination so it resolves to the Insights library or an approved reports index.
Provide one reusable landing-page template and a prioritized migration list for the next three reports. Migration of those reports is not included.
Perform read-only validation of crawlability, schema syntax, canonical metadata and visible attribution after implementation by the approved site owner.
explicit_exclusions: No website redesign, CMS rebuild or broad copy rewrite.
No Wikipedia creation, paid link building, PR campaign or social-media management.
No guarantee of rankings, AI citations, traffic, enquiries, partnerships or revenue.
No publication, deployment, DNS, hosting or production mutation without separate approval and access.
No contract-value, budget, signing-authority or named-buyer assumption.
No representation that CEEFM remains an active client.

proof.approved_claim: CEEFM GEO score moved from 16 to 77 between the engagement start and the 2026-06-10 audit.
proof.usage_rule: Describe it only as the CEEFM engagement, March to June 2026. Never call it a completed 16-week engagement or an active client.
proof.fit: It is registered as strong proof for the Content, Visibility & Demand route and demonstrates BridgeWorks can improve machine-readable visibility foundations.

likely_contact_route.buyer_role_hypothesis: The owner of research publishing, corporate communications or digital presence

dependencies: GBS confirms the authoritative author, publication date, legal or trading identity and official profile URLs.
GBS or its site owner can implement the approved specification or separately authorize BridgeWorks to do so.
The original PDF remains available at a stable approved URL.
acceptance_criteria: The pilot report has a crawlable HTML page with visible author, date, summary, key findings and PDF link.
The page has a self-referencing canonical and syntactically valid structured data using approved facts only.
Organization markup distinguishes the official gbsafrica.co.uk entity using approved identifiers and sameAs links.
The Reports navigation no longer resolves to a 404.
A reusable page specification and prioritized next-three-report list are delivered.
No outcome outside BridgeWorks control is promised.
what_would_invalidate_or_weaken: GBS already has equivalent HTML report pages or structured entity markup not visible in the audited public site.
The current research library is not used for authority, partnership or market-development goals.
GBS cannot confirm report authorship, dates or official entity identifiers.
No internal owner can implement or authorize the pilot.
The UK entity and operating brand cannot be reconciled sufficiently to publish accurate Organization markup.
entry_offer.commercial_framing: Help one current GBS Africa report become a citable web authority asset, then use the result to decide whether the wider library deserves migration. Do not sell a broad GEO transformation.

artifact_decision.artifact: one-page GEO visibility and research-citability teaser
artifact_decision.why_it_materially_improves_outreach: The problem is technical and the contact route is general. A one-page visual can show the current PDF-only journey, the missing attribution and entity layer, and the proposed pilot page without asking the recipient to accept an abstract GEO claim.

short_outreach_draft.subject: Your 2026 research is harder to cite than it should be
short_outreach_draft.body:
Hello GBS Africa team,

I reviewed how Africa Prospects 2026 and the wider Insights library appear on the web. The research is current and substantial, but each item routes directly to a PDF, with no citable HTML page, and the site gives search and AI systems limited structured context to distinguish the firm from another business using the GBS Africa name.

BridgeWorks has a bounded pilot for one flagship report: a citable landing page, clear authorship, entity markup and a reusable pattern for later reports. During the CEEFM engagement, March to June 2026, its GEO score moved from 16 to 77.

May I send the one-page findings to the person responsible for research publishing or digital presence?

Emmanuel
BridgeWorks
